summary: Best val_bpb 1.005200 (commit 030af2e) vs the 1.012347 starting point, from three stacked changes: dim 768 -> 512 at depth 8 (1.010895), passing buffer_size=192 instead of the default 1000 to make_dataloader so its O(B*buffer_size) pure-Python best-fit packing scan stops stalling every step (1.006761, +7.5% steps), and syncing the GPU once per 4 steps instead of twice per step (1.005200, 346.6M tokens). The dominant fact is that this setup is per-step-overhead-bound, not FLOP-bound: MFU is only ~28%, so model shape is nearly flat (head_dim 64 vs 128 cost 0.002, and shrinking width bought little), while anything that removes per-step cost pays off. What did not work: a background prefetch thread for the dataloader (GIL contention, 1594 vs 2398 steps, 1.034067) and halving tokens/step to 2^16 (1.032114, only +41% steps for half the tokens). Next I would attack the remaining ~48ms/step of GPU-side fixed cost - cudagraphs via torch.compile(mode='reduce-overhead') and the fp32 logits/softcap/cross-entropy chain over 131k x 8192, which is what makes peak VRAM 22.7GB - and only then revisit LR.
